claims.name: Overlapping multipolar relationships
claims.detail: India cooperates through Quad while retaining Russia–BRICS engagement. Multiple powers bargain across forums instead of strict bipolar assignment.
claims.test: Track whether cross-institution participation survives acute strategic disputes.

claims.name: Controlled engagement / multi-alignment
claims.detail: India continues Quad participation and BRICS/Russia engagement, making this a concrete case of the manuscript’s India-based analogy.
claims.test: Measure sustained diplomatic and economic participation across competing institutional groupings.

claims.name: Plural regional diplomacy à la ASEAN
claims.detail: ASEAN and China maintain prolonged code-of-conduct discussions; disagreement on binding status shows the difficulty of translating dialogue into enforceable rules.
claims.test: Has a legally effective and enforceable code been adopted and implemented?

claims.name: Diversify dependence to limit coercion
claims.detail: EU phased removal of Russian gas, Quad critical-minerals and fuel work show diversification as an actual strategy. This supports risk-management logic, not the wider cross-bloc integration outcome.
claims.test: Document dependency concentration and whether diversification measurably reduces leverage.

claims.name: Regional security architecture matters beyond borders
claims.detail: The 2026 war negotiations encompass broader European security and NATO assurances, consonant with CCC’s wider framing, without implying any legitimisation of territorial conquest.
claims.test: Does an agreed settlement address enforceable regional guarantees and independent sovereignty?

claims.name: Institutionalised mediation and confidence measures
claims.detail: Abu Dhabi talks and a reported prospective prisoner exchange illustrate negotiation, but not a durable impartial institutional system.
claims.test: Permanent, independently monitored arrangements with meaningful participation of affected parties.

claims.name: Port and corridor infrastructure as geopolitical assets
claims.detail: Quad port plans and OECD IMEC analysis confirm the importance of shared port and corridor governance as strategic concerns.
claims.test: Actual cross-border governance and transparent benefit sharing, not solely plans and funds.

claims.name: Russia–Europe economic convergence
claims.detail: EU gas imports from Russia fell sharply and a phased EU import ban was adopted. Cross-rival economic re-integration is not the observed trajectory.
claims.test: Reciprocal, legally anchored market access and energy commitments spanning Russia and Western-aligned states.

claims.name: Strategic equidistance in Central/Eastern Europe
claims.detail: Finland and Sweden entered NATO and Ukraine has advanced EU accession, indicating convergence on European alliances in this geographic setting.
claims.test: Durable sovereign participation in a nonexclusive third forum without weakening current alliances.

claims.name: CCC-style inclusive institution established
claims.detail: No verified CCC founding convention, treaty ratification, dispute mechanism or cross-bloc pilot infrastructure operating under the proposed charter.
claims.test: Convention, ratification, a functioning secretariat and pilots approved by participating states.

claims.name: Great-power resistance to shared governance
claims.detail: Debates over who is represented at EU security talks and at a possible US–China–Russia meeting echo the manuscript’s concerns about institutional inclusivity and unequal leverage.
claims.test: Do affected smaller states gain binding decision rights rather than post-hoc consultation?

claims.name: Incremental pilots precede diplomatic convergence
claims.detail: Quad and IMEC produce sector-based cooperation and coordination structures, but largely among selected partners rather than between strategic rivals.
claims.test: Pilots crossing competing alignments that demonstrate reciprocal costs and gains.
